To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cosmic variances for the best unbiased estimator of the third moment and the best unbiased estimator of the bispectrum are, respectively, $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the cosmic variances of the corresponding Gaussian quantities.

the best unbiased estimator for the CMB third moments is a linear combination of all the CMB anisotropities, with weights that depend on the harmonic space location of the latter; the best unbiased estimator of the CMB angular trispectrum is a quadratic combination of the CMB anistropities, with coefficients that depend on the location in the harmonic space of the latter.

the best unbiased estimator for the CMB third-moment is given by the sum of the three terms (i) the CMB third-order moments, (ii) the product of the CMB second-order moments, (iii) a term that is a function of the CMB power spectrum and the CMB third moments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of the best unbiased estimator for the third moment of the CMB anisotropy.
the best possible extraction of the three-point correlator of the CMB anisotropropies from the observational data.
the construction of best unbiased estimators that can be used in the detection of non-Gaussiantiy in CMB maps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best unbiased estimator for the CMB third-moment cosmic variance is larger than that of the CMB angular-bispectrum cosmic variance by about 30%.

the best unbiased estimator of the third moment is the one based on the spherical harmonics decomposition of the field, while for the angular bispectrum the best estimator is the one based only on the multipoles of the bispectrum, which are the spherical harmonics coefficients of a field defined as the product of two fields.
, in the case of the CMB third moments, the best unbiased estimator is the standard one, while for the CMB bispectrum the best unbiased estimator depends on the particular configuration of interest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the CMB third moments and the CMB bispectrum, the best estimators are not the standard estimators.

, for a given number of modes, the cosmic variance of the bispectrum estimator is smaller by about one order of magnitude than the cosmic variance of a third moment estimator, while the signal-to-noise ratio is larger by about one order for the bispectrum than for the third moment.
the best unbiased estimator for the bispectrum is not the same as the best unbiased estimator for the third moment and vice versa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cosmic variance of the bispectrum can be reduced by a factor of about 3 with respect to the cosmic variance of a single moment.
for both estimators, the cosmic variance noise is of order $N_{\rm pix}^{-1}$, which means that the signal-to-noise ratio is of order $\sqrt{N_{\rm eff}}$.
the best unbiased estimator for the CMB third moments has a much smaller cosmic variance than the best unbiased estimator for the CMB bispectrum.
